route: exemption: explicit code labels in the paper, corroborated by route 1 (per-item discrimination vs published loadings)
evidence: Paper Table 3 prefixes each item with the code FB1-FB9 used by the S1 CSV headers. Codebook-flagged reverse-worded items {3,5,7,8} intercorrelate +0.19..+0.46 and run 0 to -0.17 against forward items (e.g. AOT4 vs AOT3/5/7/8 = -0.11/-0.17/-0.09/-0.09), while forward items {1,2,4,6,10} intercorrelate +0.05..+0.25 — exactly the codebook's reverse-coding assignment. Means are semantically coherent (AOT5 'Changing your mind is a sign of weakness' = 1.20, lowest; AOT10 'consider more than one possible answer' = 4.50, highest). Reverse-copy mapping confirmed exactly: AOT3 88/205/68/111/35 vs AOT3_rev 35/111/68/205/88; AOT5 308/151/23/14/11 vs AOT5_rev 11/14/23/151/308; same for 7 and 8.

Block means match Pennycook et al. (2015): BSR items mean 2.32 (range 2.06-2.68) rated less profound than MOT motivational quotations mean 3.09 (range 2.72-3.47), n=507 per item. This confirms the BSR/MOT block assignment but not the ordering within each block; within-block order needs no inference because the codebook keys wording to the exact source column names the processing script carries through unchanged. No per-item published statistics were located to test within-block order.
